title: d-9: cron-app-storage
description:
## Deliverables
1. Implement CronStore<S:Storage<CronRow> + Storage<MontyBlobRow>> and CronStorage ONCE in sc-cron using the generic atomic unit. Implement only the domain CronStorage surface; keep the underlying Storage<CronRow> backend private and map its typed failures to CronError. Every public storage function implemented or changed here in CronStore/CronStorage, migration and cron-command storage adapters must return a typed Result and must not panic (ANC-035). Own CronRow mapping/schema, active-name/row-limit admission, per-row generation checks, fenced record_run/set_next/stop/disable and atomic set_enabled_many/replace_and_set_enabled — REQ-CRON-0004/0020/0021; ANC-030/031/033/034.
2. Migrate scheduler/worker to awaited app-supplied storage, porting hooks to the single sc-monty interpreter, preserving clock-driven tick dispatch, in-flight skip, cooperative stop/cancellation and typed FENCED behavior. Existing record_run and set_next still persist execution outcomes and next-run state through the fenced atomic policy operations in deliverable1. Domain read/check/mutate runs in one serializable atomic body, never separate calls. Backend is table-neutral — ADR-RUN-0013/0014/0020.
3. Implement legacy cron.db-to-app-DB migration above generic storage: preserve IDs/generation/run/end/spec/hook state; idempotent import and collision/rollback refusal. Legacy source is read only as explicit migration input, no ongoing second database setting — REQ-CRON-0004.
4. Reuse the ported async CronStorage conformance suite owned here against its double; port, never delete, existing assertions. Retire legacy DB files/dependency only after generic suite has equivalent case IDs and double tests pass. Actual engine/two-process provider runs are d-11, not a false double claim. Adapt thin cron-command APIs and READMEs. Inspect the resolved normal/build dependency graphs of both sc-cron and sc-cron-commands: neither may contain any crate from the sc-compose repository except permitted sc-sha, and neither may contain an ATM crate. Dev-only test/benchmark references are outside this production rule; use inspection evidence, with no new checker — REQ-RUN-0702; ANC-061/035.


5. Ask sc-monty to compile the source when a schedule is submitted or updated, rejecting invalid source before any tick. Persist the just-compiled, never-run session blob through Storage<MontyBlobRow> in a sc-cron-owned table. Key it by SHA-256 of the exact source computed with permitted sc-sha, plus the Monty dump version. The schedule source remains authoritative; use a blob only for a matching key. Missing/stale/corrupt/unreadable-version blobs or missing cron_stop/cron_tick are cache misses: recompile from source and overwrite with the pre-run dump. Persist no run/session execution state. Migrate the new cron-owned table through generic row/schema APIs; no storage backend acquires cron SQL/types. — owner item 2.
6. Replace sc-cron's Monty compile/session/limits/host/dump/load implementation with calls to sc-monty. Keep JSON conversion, cron hook names/policy and schedule payload handling here; hooks continue receiving values, never JSON strings. Preserve all copied/ported unit and integration assertions. A schedule accepts Monty or Python script plus JSON data; keep that data available to the app transform before policy-checked persistence. — owner items 1/5, single-implementation and copy rulings.

## Boundaries and handoffs
Full real-SQLite/mixed-engine cron conformance is d-11, actual released beads-cache d-12. No storage backend imports sc-cron or specific table code. No separate duplicate cron invariant suite. Hand the completed sc-cron-commands files/tests/README/manifest to d-11 for shared-path routing after this sprint sanity; d-11 consumes this policy API and d-10 common helpers in its existing final integration wave.
CronStore consumes AtomicStorage::transaction(spec, producer) from the shared Storage<T> contract; d-6/d-7/d-8 implement that same method for SQLite/Postgres/MySQL, while d-9 supplies only cron policy bodies (ANC-033).
Retire ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and legacy SQLite files in0.3.0, updating lib.rs/row.rs/storage.rs after the d-5 handoff. CronStore wraps Storage<CronRow> privately and exposes only policy-checked CronStorage operations. Keep per-name in-flight behavior and generation fencing under local REQ-CRON-0001 and ADR-RUN-0013; upstream crosswalk numbers are provenance, not local requirement IDs.
Convert every remaining registry line in crates/sc-cron/Cargo.toml and every registry line in crates/sc-cron-commands/Cargo.toml, including dev/optional entries, to >= tested floors with no upper bound; preserve features. This includes async-trait, chrono, cron, getrandom, tokio, tracing, process-wrap, sc-monty, sc-sha, tempfile and libc; remove direct monty/monty-types dependencies after the shared-interpreter port, plus utoipa >=6.0.0 and schemars >=1.2.3 in sc-cron-commands (ANC-037). The sc-cron Windows declarations inherited from d-5 are win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0, each with no upper bound; retain those already-open requirements unchanged.

After the d-5 boundary registration handoff, own boundaries/sc-cron/sc-cron.toml for the actual public-facade/root removals matching this implementation. This is the boundary's own facade, not a shared root registry.

sc-monty compilation/dump or cache-miss reconstruction is requested before the atomic storage body; interpreter work is not awaited inside that body. Persist the validated schedule/blob through the generic atomic operation while retaining admission/fencing checks (owner item 2; ANC-033).

Shared-command handoff: cron.start and cron.end use storage_write, cron.list uses storage_read when d-11 integrates d-10 helpers. These are all user-facing cron commands. Consume d-5's passing exact copy of the current Monty code AND unit/integration tests before extending or moving the cron adapter; retain every hook assertion (ANC-062).

The complete cron command set is: cron.start uses storage_write; cron.end uses storage_write; cron.list uses storage_read. Every cron command uses the shared path. No cron command is excluded (ANC-053/054).

Every compile, session run, session dump/load and host-function dispatch requested by sc-cron is executed only by sc-monty. sc-cron only selects source/cache entries, converts JSON to Monty values and supplies cron-specific value adapters; it contains no interpreter compiler, session runner or host dispatcher of its own (ANC-041).

Own sc-cron-commands/Cargo.toml dependency registration for the later library policy adapter, including sc-storage from the d-5 workspace registration at >=0.2.0 during development and >=0.3.0 at release, with no upper bound in either case. Existing sc-command/sc-cron dependencies support d-11 source integration; d-11 adds no dependency or manifest edit. This manifest passes from d-9 directly to d-12 for final release-version lines on their existing dependency path.
design:
Consumes real CronStorage/row/operation-context and generic atomic declarations from d-5. Own the single tests/support/cron-storage provider suite, ported from existing cron assertions; scheduler double runs here, actual engines in d-11. D-5 supplies only generic storage doubles without cron rows. Domain functions are transaction-safe-marked callees: active-name/row-count/read, mutate and write are one transaction, per-row (id,generation) preserves FENCED. Serializability/retry belongs to engine; caller supplies fresh-body producer with owned immutable inputs, not external I/O. No backend-specific SQL/type/schema enters generic engines; cron mapping and migration remain in sc-cron.
Current legacy DB tests/assertions are mapped to shared conformance before deletion, checked by executing the suite and retaining its cases, not by waiting for sibling d-6. d-5 has already qualified legacy code on0.41 and handed implementation files to this owner. Remove direct rusqlite only when generic CronStore and migration consumer compile. Keep upstream crosswalk REQ-CRON-0001; ADR-RUN-0013 meanings alongside local requirements; no repository-wide API sync lease is added.
Public APIs changed by this phase return typed Results without panics; storage submission follows root writer constraints. Deferred synchronization/permissions/code generation remain out of scope. Contract ratification status is defined once by d-5 and enforced at d-12 publication.
Windows manifest counterpart: d-5 alone converts sc-cron/Cargo.toml win32job/waitpid-any dev-dependency pins to open tested floors; d-9 takes the manifest later but retains both already-open >= requirements with no upper bound and their purpose comments (ANC-037).
acceptance_criteria:
boundary:sc-cron — Shared generic CronStorage conformance passes on the controlled double; scheduler hook/Monty/clock/cancellation and command-adapter regressions pass. All current behavior cases are ported, not weakened/deleted. Per-row FENCED, configured row limits, active-name and multi-row operations are implemented once through named generic transactions, with owned replayable inputs and transaction-safe bodies.
boundary:sc-cron/migration — Controlled legacy-row snapshot imports preserve every field; second invocation is idempotent, collisions/errors are typed and atomic. No default cron.db setting or store constructor. Public changed storage APIs are Result-returning/no-panic; no caller storage block_on/spawn_blocking bridge. READMEs match actual API; every registry requirement in sc-cron/sc-cron-commands uses >= its tested floor with no upper bound (ANC-037).
Required: cargo test -p sc-cron -p sc-cron-commands; shared conformance against double; normal Monty tests; cargo build --workspace at this closure; sc-lint lint sc-boundary --root . --config sc-lint.toml; sc-lint#931 no-panic rule and the external transaction-body analyzer must pass on this sprint's changed storage code once delivered; until both rules exist and pass, closure stays blocked. Record the actual rule versions and commands when available, never a fabricated pass or implicit waiver. This includes sc-cron CronStore/CronStorage, migration and changed sc-cron-commands storage adapters. d-11 executes same suite with actual engine providers and deterministic two-process scenarios; this sprint never calls the double real database proof.
boundary:sc-cron/row-limit — CronStore refuses to add a schedule row once its row count reaches the embedding application's configured limit; the existing row-limit tests are ported, not deleted (ANC-031).
boundary:sc-cron/atomic — set_enabled_many, replace_and_set_enabled and every domain read/check/mutate body call the shared generic transaction operation; several row operations commit or roll back as one atomic unit (ANC-033).
boundary:sc-cron/active-name — Within the SAME AtomicStorage::transaction body, CronStore rejects a second active schedule row with the same schedule name; retain and pass the ported active-name tests against the controlled double (ANC-030).
boundary:sc-cron/public-storage-functions — The public CronStorage domain operations (create/get/list_active, record_run/set_next/stop/disable, set_enabled/set_enabled_many/replace_and_set_enabled, query/context), migration and storage adapters all return typed Results and do not panic. These are the public storage functions governed by ANC-035, NFR-RUN-0009 and REQ-CRON-0005; exercise their typed-error paths through the shared conformance tests and actual sc-lint#931 rule, with no missing-rule waiver (NFR-RUN-0002).
boundary:sc-cron/ADR-RUN-0011 — sc-cron and sc-cron-commands production code, including CronStore/CronStorage, migration, scheduler/worker and cron-command adapters, calls no Runtime::block_on, Handle::block_on or futures::executor::block_on. Required: python3 scripts/adr_run_0011_grep.py crates/sc-cron/src crates/sc-cron-commands/src; non-test sources must contain no block_on call or allow-comment exemption. The only ADR-RUN-0011 exception is Runtime::block_on on the SQLite writer dedicated thread, which this sprint does not own.
boundary:sc-cron/policy-entry — No raw public CronStore write bypasses active-name, row-limit or fenced-generation policy; the same domain suite exercises all mutation entry points. Mapped StorageError retains typed code/source/recovery alongside stable CronError codes.
boundary:sc-cron/compiled-monty — Using the real shared interpreter and controlled storage, submit rejects non-compiling source; successful writes dump immediately after compile, before execution. Restart reloads an unchanged source/version blob without recompiling. Source/version mismatch, missing/corrupt bytes and missing cron_stop/cron_tick each trigger source recompilation and overwrite. Assert source remains authoritative, the key uses sc-sha SHA-256 plus dump version, and no post-run state is persisted. The new row/table and migration belong only to sc-cron, with no table-specific backend change. Port existing hook/host/limits/integration tests without weakening them; value inputs and JSON conversion behavior remain unchanged.

boundary:cron-manifest-floors — At closure verify every registry requirement in the complete sc-cron and sc-cron-commands manifests, including normal/dev/optional/target-specific entries, is >= its tested floor with no upper bound. Verify inherited Windows win32job >=2.0.3 and waitpid-any >=0.3.0 declarations too; prior d-5 ownership does not exempt them from this check. Those two already-open declarations remain unchanged. Use inspection evidence of the owned manifests; add no checking code, checker or dependency edge (ANC-037; owner one-checker rule).
notes:
authored from docs/prd/sc-runtime-prd.md and ADR0020/0021@a6cc949bafa9e7f1817f4514a19328c3021ffc42; B selected via lead01M76Q2R5JRAE3AA9NVBEF1HG4, placement/service cut via01M76Q74CR889863W7EHRW2A14; original d-1/d-3 work folded into named owners, no overlapping A sprint
Boundary closure is sc-cron. The small sc-cron-commands edits are pass-through API/bound adaptations folded here to avoid a thin sprint; they are not a separately closed cross-crate feature. d-11 owns actual command-adapter/service/transport composition behavior. Scheduler contract tests use the controlled storage double; preserve all existing adapter regressions.

dependencies.title: Phase D: shared app storage, channel writer and published consumer migration
dependencies.description:
Phase D makes the SDK easy to adopt and lets consumers choose dependency upgrades. Product intent is PRD v2.0; the release is the owner-selected nine public crates at0.3.0. Generic backends contain no consumer table code. Sprint metadata.owned_paths is the authoritative full file fence; summaries below are navigation only.

| Sprint | Wave | Boundary | Consumed artifacts |
|---|---|---|---|
| d-3 | 1 | dependency/source compatibility | none; owns the one manifest checker |
| d-4 | 1 | generation tooling | none |
| d-5 | 1 | storage/atomic/row contract + standalone sc-monty | none; owner ratification and Active ADR0020/0021 before consumers |
| d-6 | 2 | SQLite backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-7 | 2 | Postgres backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-8 | 2 | MySQL backend | d-5 production contract |
| d-9 | 2 | cron domain adapter | d-5 production contract and additive legacy build |
| d-10 | 2 | common commands/transforms | d-3 compiled command server/schema/error ABI, d-5 Storage/row contract |
| d-11 | 3 | generated composition | d-3 checker, d-4 tools, d-6/7/8/9/10 code |
| d-12 | 3 | registry migration/release/recommendations | d-3 source/checker, d-4 tools, d-6/9/10 code; d-11 completion checked before upload |

Ten sprints; critical path3, width6. No dependency exists solely because two sprints edit the same manifest. The release and generated-integration sprints prepare in parallel; upload waits for completed generated integration. No implementation dispatch before plan approval.
dependencies.design:
PRD v2.0 governs product scope. sc-storage is std-only; storage/atomic/row traits are the shared contract, with phase-d transaction name/mode properties and room for later per-transaction retry policy. SQLite uses one async queue and one writer thread exclusively owning its sole write-mode connection, queued writes commit together, and replies follow commit. Only the writer runtime uses Runtime::block_on. Readers use blocking_recv without a runtime; async callers never block or use spawn_blocking to submit writes. Consumer rows/schema/migrations stay above generic engines. sc-cron implements its policy once over generic atomic Storage<CronRow> and keeps raw backend mutation out of the CronStore public facade.

D-5 owns contract types, shared registry/boundary definitions, required REQ/ADR amendments and the minimal legacy compatibility build. Its layer-file handoffs are additive contract/legacy artifacts on existing dependencies, not simultaneous same-wave edits. d-9 owns the0.3.0 removal of ScheduleStore/SqliteScheduleStore and obsolete SQLite files after those artifacts compile. Root Cargo.toml passes directly from d-5 registrations to d-12 release-version conversion; d-6 reads it. d-3 owns the command manifest with its rmcp3.9 server/schema compatibility code; d-10 consumes that compiled artifact and later adds storage helpers. Specific crate facade boundaries pass from d-5 to their implementation owner on the existing must-follow edges.

D-5 owner ratification is pending and gates its closure; ADR0020/0021 must be Active before d-6..d-12 start. The actual no-panic rule sc-lint#931 and transaction-safe analyzer remain required for affected owner-sprint closure and are rechecked before publication. Lead owns the external analyzer request; missing delivery is a real blocker, not a waiver.

D-3 owns the sole interim SDK manifest checker; d-11 invokes it on generated outputs and d-12 on exact archives/upload. Remove it after equivalent sc-lint#936 release/adoption. Published/template registry requirements are open tested floors (ANC-037); normal tests check the selected versions, with no dedicated min/latest jobs. Consumers may pin what they want. D-12 alone produces the final newest-tested Cargo.lock recommendation and matching .sc-runtime/tested-dependencies.json (ANC-038).

Nine published packages at0.3.0: sc-storage, sc-runtime-db-sqlite, sc-config, sc-transport, sc-command, sc-runtime, sc-cron, sc-cron-commands, sc-monty. Postgres/MySQL generic engines remain generated this phase under that approved packaging scope; their implementation fixes need template updates/regeneration, explicitly recorded in ADR0020. They do not acquire an invented library-upgrade guarantee. D-12 derives publication order from actual manifests, sc-monty/sc-storage in the first wave, rehearses exact archives, then proves actual upstream beads-cache PR open/CI green against registry crates. Its independent preparation does not upload until d-11 sanity is closed and completed composition merged, with ratification and actual safety rules passing. Missing release predicates leave publication open.

The phase is one append-only stack with one writer. Metadata layer is planned presentation order; actual link order follows completion. pr_target is the consumed lower bound, not false sibling serialization. Canonical root Cargo.lock is d-12-owned. Historical probe facts remain in Git/review evidence, not a second live scope document.


## Boundary map and generated targets
Read existing boundaries/<crate>/<crate>.toml. sc-config dependencies serde/serde_json unchanged; sc-transport tokio/reqwest/serde->sc-runtime unchanged; sc-command gains sc-storage, consumers sc-cron/sc-cron-commands/sc-runtime; sc-runtime composes transport/command, no storage trait placement there; sc-cron loses direct SQLite backend, depends on sc-storage/sc-command; sc-cron-commands adapts scheduler. Generic writer dependencies sc-storage/rusqlite/Tokio only, NEVER sc-cron/ATM/sc-compose; no consumer SQL/schema. New boundaries/sc-storage/sc-storage.toml has no sc-* dependency. Generated store/service boundaries are emitted by template/boundaries/render.py at boundaries/<prefixed-package>/<prefixed-package>.toml with existing Store/Stores facades; no invented static template boundaries. Application row descriptors/migrations are supplied at open, engine applies them before exposing store.

Wave-1 d-5 delivers the single sc-monty implementation, first copying current code and all unit/integration tests exactly and passing them before extension. Its production dependencies are only pydantic Monty crates; sc-cron owns cron/JSON adapters and source-keyed compiled-session blobs via generic Storage rows, sc-sha is permitted. d-11 follows the existing d-9/d-10 prerequisites to route cron.start/end/list through common helpers and a library-owned policy adapter, without bypassing CronStorage or requiring app-written actions. Transform sources load at run time, default conversion needs no hand-written transform, and the provisional0.3.0 seam preserves future second-input/no-write/atomic-transform options without building them.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria:
1. d-11 closes actual generated SQLite app/cron shared database/channel writer, real typed transforms/CRUD and all selected engines/mixed layouts; no vulnerable SQLx SQLite or separate cron.db default, no fake engine proof.
2. d-12 closes actual upstream migration PR open/CI-green at exact SHA against nine published0.3.0 crates; no path/patch/Git SDK substitute. All source/package/API/docs and normal test suites pass.
3. Generic backends contain no consumer table code; named owned retryable atomic API and static+runtime safety checks actually operate. Public changed storage APIs return typed errors/no panic; writer panic fails every waiting caller. External rule and ratification blockers stay explicit until met.
4. All existing workspace/lint/test/boundary/publishing-kit/controlled-host benchmark gates pass; publication waits for closed d-11 sanity and owner ratification, after exact archive rehearsal. Required coverage and independent plan/development gates are separate from schema validation.
